#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done

content.text:
I added the per-period cut history, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Each pool member's line now shows a `pool-cut-<period>` value for every period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today. The value is the member's cut as it stood at the end of that period, and it's blank when there was none: no pool or member yet, the pool unbalanced, no pot, or the membership dates not covering that day.

**How it works:** the app already saves a copy of each sheet after every change, under the day it was made. It also has a read-only "as of a date" view that shows the sheet as it stood on that day. So I didn't need any server, schema or audit changes. All the changes are in the front end:

- **`features/pools/pools.ts`**:
  - The cut calculation is now a standalone function, `poolFigures`, so today's cuts and past cuts use exactly the same rules (holds, retirement, membership dates, nested pools, how the remainder is shared out).
  - When the pools are read, the screen also reads the periods. For each period that has ended, it reads the pools, people and pot as of the period's to-date and works out the cuts with that day as the sheet's today.
  - Past members are matched to today's by pool id and by person or member-pool id.
- **`core/as-of.interceptor.ts`**: a request that sets its own as-of date now keeps it. Before, a screen that was itself in as-of mode would have overwritten it.

**Limitations:**
- **Speed:** each ended period adds three as-of reads, and the server handles a sheet's as-of reads one at a time. On a sheet with many periods, the pools section will take noticeably longer to load.
- **Staleness:** the history is re-read when the sheet is loaded or its today changes. Adding a period that has already ended shows its cuts only after the next reload.
